motivation_or_inadequacy: A static positive factorization can reproduce one observation while failing to admit positive stochastic updates for repeated supplied transformations. The candidate seeks to measure the information loss caused by insisting that the same finite state set support every successive positive update.
object_definition: For a compact group G with normalized Haar measure, an orthogonal representation pi:G->O(V), and m-state row-stochastic action-dependent kernels P_g, define (A_P z)_i = integral_G pi(g)^(-1)(sum_j P_g(i,j)z_j) dg on V^m with norm max_i ||z_i||. Define kappa_m(pi) = sup_{||v||=1} sup_{||w_j||=1} integral_G max_j <w_j,pi(g)v> dg. Its dual action on unnormalized conditional means contracts the sum of their norms. The candidate is the paired transfer/contraction interface, not a claim that either constituent is historically new.
primitive_operations: Encode a current group action and its positive stochastic transition in the same representation-valued transfer rather than averaging the transition alone.
Compose transfer operators for successive controls while retaining their action correlation.
Bound loss in unnormalized conditional means by the orbit-code coefficient kappa_m(pi).
For non-Haar control laws, apply the coefficient to k-step product laws to form a block retention profile.
consistency_conditions: G is compact and integration uses normalized Haar measure for the stated kappa_m(pi).
pi is an orthogonal representation of G on the declared finite-dimensional real inner-product space V.
Each P_g is row-stochastic on the same m-state space and measurable in the supplied control.
Controls are independent under the Haar contraction theorem; the finite-law block result uses the declared independent product law.
All persistent classical information is represented in the finite Markov state; external correlated randomness and stored continuous controls are charged or excluded.
relations_to_existing_mathematics: The sphere coefficient is a constrained spherical quantization quantity with established geometric literature.
The transfer is representation-valued and is related to familiar representation transforms; the source disclaims inventing that transform.
The full-unitary coefficient depends on conjugation orbits and Grassmannian small-ball geometry.
Convex geometry and barycentric positive realizations provide the matching construction.

Source-reported full-unitary state count Theta_(D,delta,epsilon)(T^(D-1)) for fixed D and the specified weak-measurement process; static positive factorization size D^2.
A finite-control block profile and explicit limits on transferring continuous-Haar conclusions to finite alphabets.

counterexamples_and_failure_scope: Signed affine coordinates can compose exactly while some entries are negative; this does not meet the positive-stochastic model and blocks a blanket claim about numerical computation.
Correlated external noise can act as extra persistent memory and changes the charged model.
Finite groups can have bounded-state exact realizations; the continuous-control lower bound does not automatically transfer.
For support size at most m, the one-step finite-law coefficient is 1; a proposed fixed five-gate Theta(T) law is unresolved in this investigation and is not claimed globally open.

exact_contract.domain: Finite-dimensional real inner-product representation spaces; sphere rotations SO(d); full-unitary conjugation on traceless Hermitian D by D matrices.
exact_contract.norms_or_metrics: V^m uses max_i ||z_i||; conditional means use sum_i ||b_i||. Full unitary uses Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Output criterion is uniform additive error in binary probability.
